_note: ALL numbers in this file are ASSUMPTIONS unless a 'source' says they come from quantum_arch or a cited reference. They are illustrative inputs of a scenario model for the mid-2030s, not forecasts, quotes or measurements. Entries flagged 'FROM quantum_arch' are read from quantum_arch at run time, not stored here.

challenge.note: Challenge constraints (image 1.png). Earth-only: launches, orbit, Moon and Mars are NOT modelled (launch cost kept in the config only so a later extension has a place for it).

engine.tick_note: Time resolution: the engine advances in fixed ticks (default 60 s). Task arrivals, completions, QPU calibration windows, failures and cap changes are EVENTS with exact times (a heap); the scheduler runs, and fluid demand and power are sampled, once per tick (state at tick start, piecewise-constant over the tick).
engine.network_overhead_note: Site network and support power as a fraction of IT (system boundary) power. ASSUMPTION; quantum_arch's datacenter model uses 0.08 for its own illustrative cases.
engine.rho_slo_note: Highest module utilisation at which the mass-LLM traffic still meets its SLO (headroom for bursts). ASSUMPTION; quantum_arch baselines use 0.7 as its default operating point.
engine.model_cost_note: Per-token compute and memory-traffic cost of the SERVED model relative to quantum_arch's 70B-class reference (llm_inference_70b). 10 stands for a frontier-class sparse model with long reasoning traces. ASSUMPTION, large uncertainty.
engine.fluid_displace_note: Penalty used by the optimising policies when a discrete task takes GPU modules the mass traffic needs (shed demand costs revenue and breaks SLOs). ASSUMPTION.

decision_latency.note: Modelled decision latency of the single scheduling node (not wall-clock): decisions take effect this many seconds after the tick.

engine.network_note: WAN egress cost, intra-site bandwidth and the user-edge bandwidth per transfer. ASSUMPTIONS.

cooling._note: pue = pue_base + pue_per_k * max(0, T_ambient - free_cooling_c). rack_kw_limit caps the system power of one rack (rack density effect: modules per rack = min(node max, limit / module system power)). capex_usd_per_kw_it = building + power + cooling plant per kW of the site's power cap. ALL ASSUMPTIONS (orders of magnitude from public 2024-26 build-cost ranges, extrapolated).

node_types._note: kind gpu/lpu/prefill nodes are RACKS made of 'modules' (accelerator modules). Power per module and the server overhead ratio come from quantum_arch's gpu_2035 device (FROM quantum_arch); other accelerator classes are scaled from it with the factors below (ASSUMPTIONS). speeds are relative to a GPU module (1.0).

gpu_rack.label: GPU rack (decode and prefill)
gpu_rack.capex_note: module about 70k USD plus server, network and rack overhead 60 percent: ASSUMPTION

lpu_rack.label: LPU rack (decode-optimised, SRAM-style)
lpu_rack.capex_note: ASSUMPTION: 1.6x decode tokens per module-equivalent of power, decode only; no vendor figure used

prefill_rack.label: Prefill card rack (air-coolable)
prefill_rack.capex_note: ASSUMPTION: compute-dense, low-power prefill cards, 0.6x prefill speed at 0.3x power of a module

ctxmem_pool.label: Context-memory pool (KV cache store)
ctxmem_pool.capex_note: ASSUMPTION: 5 PB flash/CXL-class KV store, 20 kW, 14 M USD

qpu_cat40k.label: QPU, 40k cat qubits (repetition code)
qpu_cat40k.capex_note: capex and calibration windows: ASSUMPTION; power, runtimes, feasibility FROM quantum_arch (mid2030s base)

qpu_annealer.label: Quantum annealer (D-Wave Advantage2 class)
qpu_annealer.capex_note: ASSUMPTION; power and sample times FROM quantum_arch annealers catalog

mixed_cat.label: Mixed node: 16 GPU modules + 40k cat-qubit QPU on a low-latency link
mixed_cat.capex_note: GPU part like gpu_rack; QPU part like qpu_cat40k plus 10 M USD for the co-location link; link latency 10 us is an ASSUMPTION

regions._note: User regions, their centroid (used for RTT = 4 ms + great-circle km / 66 per ms, fibre with a 1.5 route factor) and time-zone offset. ASSUMPTIONS.

demand._note: TWO-LEVEL MODEL. These are the FLUID classes (mass LLM traffic) - aggregate token rates per user region, never per-user simulation. Discrete tasks (task-spec files) are the second level. ALL ASSUMPTIONS. Token counts are per request/step; cached_ctx_tokens are reused from context memory on a hit and recomputed as prefill on a miss; ctx_gb is KV-cache memory per ACTIVE user session (FP8, GQA-class); active_frac is the share of users with a live session at the diurnal factor 1.

energy_price_note: Energy prices per site are in the fleet file (ASSUMPTIONS).

classical_fallback_defaults._note: ASSUMED cost of the best classical method at the SAME accuracy, in GPU-module-hours (2035 module), for the quantum_arch workloads. The scheduler compares these with quantum_arch's quantum time/energy; they are the single largest uncertainty of any quantum offload result. null = no classical method exists at that accuracy.

chemistry_small.note: same figure as quantum_arch's dc2035_research example (64 modules x 12 h), ASSUMPTION

vqe_20q.note: 2^20 state vector: trivial on one module; ASSUMPTION

qla_scalar_explicit_1m.note: sparse 1M-dimension solve: classical iterative solver is fast; quantum_arch states no advantage; ASSUMPTION

qla_scalar_implicit_1e12.note: N=2^40 with an oracle input: no classical method assumed; ASSUMPTION

femoco_thc.note: classical cost at this accuracy assumed unreachable; ASSUMPTION

shor_rsa2048.note: quantum_arch lists 6e35 classical ops: not feasible
